name: MonarchSortableGrid
title: SortableGrid
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.grid.LazyVerticalGrid with androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.detectDragGesturesAfterLongPress, LazyGridItemScope.animateItem and LazyGridState.scrollBy for auto-scroll; MonarchDragHandle for the TalkBack actions and arrow keys
summary: A grid of tiles the user reorders in two dimensions by long-pressing and dragging, with TalkBack actions and arrow keys in every direction, and every step announced.
whenToUse: For dashboards, launchers, galleries or pinned items where the person arranges tiles in rows and columns.
whenNotToUse: For a single column of rows use MonarchReorderableList. For moving items between containers use Compose drag and drop (dragAndDropSource and dragAndDropTarget).
api: @Composable public fun <T> MonarchSortableGrid(items: List<T>, key: (T) -> Any, itemLabel: (T) -> String, onReorder: (from: Int, to: Int) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, columns: Int? = null, minItemWidth: Dp = 160.dp, enabled: Boolean = true, itemEnabled: (T) -> Boolean = { true }, state: LazyGridState = rememberLazyGridState(), labels: MonarchSortableGridLabels = MonarchSortableGridLabels(), itemContent: @Composable ColumnScope.(item: T, state: MonarchSortableGridItemState) -> Unit)
public class MonarchSortableGridItemState(index: Int, dragged: Boolean, enabled: Boolean)

public class MonarchSortableGridLabels(handle: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, pickedUp: ((label: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, moved: ((label: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, dropped: ((label: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, cancelled: ((label: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, actions: Map<MonarchDragHandleDirection, String> = emptyMap())

options.name: key
options.description: A stable, unique key for an item; also the LazyVerticalGrid key.

options.name: itemLabel
options.description: The plain-text name of an item, used in the handle's name and the announcements.

options.name: onReorder
options.description: Called once per finished move (drop, action or arrow key) with the old and the new index. Move the item in items.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the grid. Give it a bounded height to make it scroll.

options.name: columns
options.description: A fixed number of columns. Without it, as many columns of minItemWidth as fit (GridCells.Adaptive).

options.name: minItemWidth
options.description: The smallest tile width for adaptive columns, multiplied by the font scale, so large text gives fewer, wider tiles.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether any tile can be moved.

options.name: itemEnabled
options.description: Whether an item can be moved. Other tiles can still move past it.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the grid.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the handle's name, the four announcements and the handle's action names.

options.name: itemContent
options.description: The content of a tile, beside the handle. The state gives the index as shown, whether the tile is dragged and whether it can move.

states.name: idle
states.description: Tiles on the surface fill with a subtle border, each with a small idle drag handle.

states.name: dragged
states.description: The held tile follows the finger above the others with the medium shadow, the accent border and a grabbed handle (Picked up); the other tiles slide out of its way.

states.name: locked tile
states.description: itemEnabled false: the handle is disabled and has no actions, and a long press does not pick it up.

states.name: disabled
states.description: enabled false: no tile can be moved.

appearance: Each tile is the surface fill with a 1dp subtle border and medium corners, the small drag handle at the start. The held tile has the medium shadow and the accent border; its handle uses the grabbed colors of MonarchDragHandle. Every color comes from the theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: The web grid follows the pointer from the handle and slides the other tiles away, and picks a tile up with Space and moves it with the arrow keys. On Android a long press anywhere on the tile picks it up, as Android launchers and grids do, and the tiles slide as on the web; TalkBack, Switch Access and hardware keyboards use the handle's four move actions and the arrow keys, which move one place at once and announce the new position. iOS shows a lifted system drag preview and moves the tile on drop, and marks the drop target with an outline (isDropTarget); Android reorders while dragging, so the item state has dragged instead of a drop target. Same type, labels and default minimum width (160dp) as iOS; the order is hoisted (from and to) instead of a binding. The web's uncontrolled defaultItems is not offered. The grid scrolls vertically only.
accessibility: Every tile has a MonarchDragHandle named Reorder and the item's label, with Move up, Move down, Move backward and Move forward (up and down only in one column); the arrow keys move the tile while the handle has focus.
Picking up, moving by an action, dropping and cancelling are announced through a polite live region: "Revenue moved to position 2 of 4."
Backward and forward follow the reading order, so they are mirrored in right-to-left layouts, and a drag follows the finger in both directions.
The held tile is shown by a border, a shadow and the grabbed handle, not by color alone.
The handle keeps a 48dp touch target; adaptive columns become fewer and wider at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: A move action past the first or last place, or above the first row or below the last, does nothing.
A drop at the place it started reports nothing to onReorder but still announces the drop.
Tiles in the same row take their own height; give the content a minimum height when tiles should line up.
The grid scrolls by at most 16dp a frame while the held tile is past its top or bottom edge.
Keys must be unique; the same key twice breaks the LazyVerticalGrid.

examples.title: Drag or keyboard in two dimensions
examples.webExample: Drag or keyboard in two dimensions
examples.template:
MonarchSortableGrid(
    items = shortcuts,
    key = { it.first },
    itemLabel = { it.second },
    onReorder = { from, to -> shortcuts.add(to, shortcuts.removeAt(from)) },
    minItemWidth = ({{minItemWidth}} * 16).dp,
    modifier = Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = {{label}} },
) { shortcut, _ ->
    MonarchText(text = shortcut.second, style = MonarchTextStyle.BodyStrong)
    MonarchText(text = shortcut.third, style = MonarchTextStyle.Caption, color = MonarchTheme.colors.textMuted)
}
examples.code:
MonarchSortableGrid(
    items = shortcuts,
    key = { it.first },
    itemLabel = { it.second },
    onReorder = { from, to -> shortcuts.add(to, shortcuts.removeAt(from)) },
    minItemWidth = (10 * 16).dp,
    modifier = Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = "Shortcuts" },
) { shortcut, _ ->
    MonarchText(text = shortcut.second, style = MonarchTextStyle.BodyStrong)
    MonarchText(text = shortcut.third, style = MonarchTextStyle.Caption, color = MonarchTheme.colors.textMuted)
}

examples.title: Adaptive columns with a pinned tile
examples.code:
MonarchSortableGrid(
    items = apps,
    key = { it },
    itemLabel = { it },
    onReorder = { from, to -> apps.add(to, apps.removeAt(from)) },
    minItemWidth = 120.dp,
    itemEnabled = { it != "Mail" },
) { app, state ->
    MonarchText(text = app)
    MonarchText(text = "Position ${state.index + 1}", style = MonarchTextStyle.Caption)
}
